name: app-context
preview: When reading the old Next.js app during migration, read this because its context and routing conventions describe legacy behavior, not requirements for the replacement.

revisions.author: 3zl47w7d-mvg8jbku-fbb69e47
revisions.body:
# Rulebook app context

The app serves player rules, GM material, and world wikis from separately compiled content. Navigation, breadcrumbs, search, and links must agree on which context is active.

**Routing priority is world, then GM, then player.** World links use `/world/{world}/{slug}`, GM links use `/gm/{slug}`, and player links use `/{slug}`. A selected world takes precedence over GM mode; the sidebar disables its GM toggle while in world context. Use the matching navigation and breadcrumb endpoints rather than mixing player data into a world page.

When touching layouts, preserve the root provider relationship: theme outside GM outside world. Theme state depends on the client and persisted browser state; account for hydration rather than moving browser-only access into server rendering. Content pages consume compiled JSON and generate known static routes where possible, while interactive navigation and search remain client-side.

The sidebar is fixed on mobile with an overlay when open and static on desktop at the `lg` breakpoint. Navigation must expand parents of the active page and handle both categorized and flat node shapes. These behaviors apply across all three content contexts, not only the player rulebook.

For content missing from an otherwise working layout, inspect the publishing stages in [[heart-rush-tools/content-pipeline]] before changing routing or rendering.

revisions.author: 3zl47w7d-mvg8jbku-fbb69e47
revisions.body:
# Legacy Next.js app context

This document describes the old `src/` application only. The replacement apps under `apps/` are not required to preserve its routes, providers, or navigation UI.

The old app serves player rules, GM material, and world wikis from separately compiled content. Its routing priority is world, then GM, then player: `/world/{world}/{slug}`, `/gm/{slug}`, and `/{slug}` respectively. A selected world takes precedence over GM mode, and the sidebar disables the GM toggle while in world context.

Its root providers nest theme outside GM outside world. Interactive navigation and search are client-side while content pages consume compiled JSON. The sidebar is fixed on mobile and static at the desktop `lg` breakpoint; categorized and flat navigation nodes share the same tree renderer.

Use this only to understand old behavior or extract content during migration. For publishing-source boundaries read [[heart-rush-tools/content-pipeline]].
revisions.rationale: The approved replacement explicitly discards old UI and routes; retain only legacy context, not preservation directives.
